title: Helper: Escape and timeouts don't cancel queued work; count/holdMs unclamped
description: Security review 2026-11-24: helper queues each request on work.async (~2544); Escape only emits an event (~2066-2071) and nothing drops queued work on stop or connection close. click count (~807) and holdMs (~823) are unclamped, so one request can run for a very long time or stall the helper for every client.
acceptance_criteria: A per-connection cancel flag drops queued and in-progress input work on Escape/stop/close; count and holdMs are clamped; a test sends a burst then stops and shows no further events.
close_reason: PR #25: not_owned/outside_app scoping, per-connection cancel generation, clamps; smoke --macos 57/57.

title: Helper: an approved pid grants screen-wide clicks and any-window screenshots
description: Security review of the kernel split (2026-11-24): the helper gates on pid only. click/scroll/drag/move post global HID events at any point outside background mode (NostringsHelper.swift ~805-834, early return ~1129), and screenshot captures any windowId with no owner check (~1998-2016). With one app approved, a script can capture other apps' windows and click into unapproved apps.
acceptance_criteria: screenshot/windowId must belong to pid; foreground pointer events authorize the app owning the target point (or are confined to pid's windows); unit/smoke checks show a cross-app capture and click are refused.
close_reason: PR #25: not_owned/outside_app scoping, per-connection cancel generation, clamps; smoke --macos 57/57.

title: Kernel split: no-privilege cell runner, privileged parent
description: Fixes ns-tzn for real. vm is no boundary: every host object (timers, ui, promises, host errors, console, inspect.custom) leaks the host Function; sandbox-exec around today's kernel is weak because it must keep open, config writes, adb 5037 and in-process Android approvals. Split: runner holds the vm context and api.mjs and talks only over stdio through a proxy backend at the backend.request seam; parent (session.mjs side) holds real backends, approvals, action log, screenshots, scripts, config, OCR, help docs, open -b. Runner: node --permission (fs-read repo only, no child, no fs-write), env {}, Seatbelt deny-default on macOS.
design: Approval already lives parent-side (Swift helper authorize; android.mjs authorize/approved), so a proxy backend keeps it. Move from runner: execFileAsync open -b (api.mjs ~629), ctx.log (parent logs from requests it sees, incl. config.log.text redaction), ctx.stop/abortReason enforcement (parent refuses requests after Escape/stop), kernel fs use (help, screenshots, scripts). Parent treats runner messages as hostile. Risks to cover: helper socket accepts any same-uid peer (getpeereid) so runner must be unable to reach the helper/daemon Unix sockets and adb 5037 (Node --permission does not cover Unix sockets before v25; Seatbelt must); approveSurface/launch take caller-supplied name/reason so dialogs are spoofable, parent/helper must own prompt text; helper 'open' is ungated, check .command/.terminal/.app targets; nested Seatbelt fails when started from a sandboxed agent shell, detect and state fallback; NOSTRINGS_APPROVAL env overrides approval mode, runner gets env {}. Node: --allow-net added in v25; below that, network denial only via Seatbelt on macOS; Linux below 25 reports 'runner not network-isolated' in doctor. Consider engines floor 22. Not for 0.6.0.
acceptance_criteria: In a cell: escape to host process via setTimeout.constructor, then file write, fetch, child_process, and connecting to the helper socket, daemon socket and adb 5037 are all denied. smoke --macos and Android emulator smoke pass. SECURITY.md describes the runner boundary and keeps saying an approved app is still code execution.
close_reason: Kernel split merged (PR #17): no-privilege runner under Seatbelt + node --permission, broker holds backends; escape test denied writes/reads/exec/net/sockets/env; smoke 7/7, smoke --macos 54/54, android 23/23 on the branch.

title: Finder rename hint omits select-all; names come out as x.txt.txt
description:
**What:** Finder's rename field selects only the base name ("draft-v1", not ".txt"), but the helper's `label_only` error and `docs/api.md` say to rename with click, `pressKey("Return")`, `typeText(name)`, `pressKey("Return")`. Following that hint turns `draft-v1.txt` into `final-report.txt.txt`. In both bench runs the agent then guessed `ctrl+a`, which on macOS moves to the start of the line, and only `super+a` fixed it.

**Evidence:** `native/macos/NostringsHelper.swift:559` and `docs/api.md:164` give the recipe without a select-all step. `bench/results/v2/transcripts.tar.gz`, finder-rename × glovebox, 2026-11-03T21-17-02 (final text: "My first attempts left the file with a doubled name") and 2026-11-03T22-22-58 (it produced "final-report.txtdraft-v1.txt"). In `bench/results/v2/summary.md` this is the one task where nostrings was not cheapest: 8.5 round trips, $0.061 and 3.5 images, against 3, $0.041 and 0 for Codex `cua_repl`.

**Why it matters:** Renaming a file in Finder is a common task. Every agent that follows the tool's own hint ends up with a wrong name, then spends round trips and screenshots fixing it.

**Done when:** The helper message, `docs/api.md` and the skill say `pressKey("cmd+a")` after `Return` (or say to type the name without its extension). Then `node bench/run.mjs --setups nostrings --tasks finder-rename --n 2` passes 2/2 with a median of 4 round trips or fewer, 0 images, and a cost under $0.041.

**Size:** small (under an hour), plus one helper rebuild and a bench run.

<!-- discovery: scout C -->
notes: Text fixed in helper label_only message, docs/api.md, SKILL.md (super+a after Return). Open until helper rebuild and bench finder-rename --n 2 run.

title: macOS background route steals focus from the user while driving Firefox
description: Report 2026-11-23 (macOS 27, Firefox 160): while an agent drove Firefox on the background route, Firefox kept taking focus from the app the user was in. Every action reported lastRoute background or accessibility, so the steal happens outside what withInputRoute checks. Suspects: app.menu('File > New Window'); app.focus on the URL bar (AXFocused); pressKey Return; pressKey super+alt+k opening an undocked DevTools window 1-3 s later (after the 60 ms check); AXPress on DevTools Console Settings; the first read setting AXEnhancedUserInterface; makeWindowKey's SLPS records reordering Firefox's windows.
design: 1. With TextEdit frontmost, run each action alone via node bin/nostrings.mjs run and log the frontmost app every 50 ms for 5 s. 2. For late activations, watch ~2 s after window-opening background actions and restore the user's app, or report it in lastRoute. 3. Smoke check: fixture opens a new window and a secondary window in the background; assert frontmost unchanged for 3 s. Also record lastRoute in actions.log.
acceptance_criteria: The new smoke check passes, and the Firefox sequence above leaves the user's app frontmost.
close_reason: Original steal not reproduced on current helper (likely fixed by AX window-number matching). Added FocusGuard + lastRoute on every action + smoke check that fails without the guard; Firefox sequence kept TextEdit frontmost. PR #21.

title: js sandbox: scripts can reach the real process and fetch
description: The kernel runs cells in a vm context, which is not a security boundary. setTimeout.constructor("return process")() returns the host process (src/kernel.mjs, context setup), and fetch is exposed to scripts. Anyone who can send a cell (the agent, or a prompt injection that reaches it) can run arbitrary code as the user, not only GUI actions. SECURITY.md now states this as a known limitation.
design: Options: run the kernel under sandbox-exec (deny network, limit file writes), drop fetch from the context, freeze/replace timer constructors. Isolation must land before any remote gateway work.
acceptance_criteria: A unit test shows setTimeout.constructor('return process')() and fetch are unavailable inside a cell, or the kernel process is sandboxed and the test shows a denied file write / network call.
notes: Staged per design review 2026-11-24: realm hardening (null-proto context, no fetch/Buffer/URL, strings:false) ships in 0.6.0 as defense in depth only. Real fix is ns-iz9 (process split). Keep open.
close_reason: Kernel split merged (PR #17): no-privilege runner under Seatbelt + node --permission, broker holds backends; escape test denied writes/reads/exec/net/sockets/env; smoke 7/7, smoke --macos 54/54, android 23/23 on the branch.

title: OCR diff after a scroll reprints almost every line as new
description: ocrDiff (src/api.mjs) matches lines by exact text plus frame, so a scroll that shifts the screen makes every line count as new or moved. On a remote-desktop viewer (a headless Linux VNC desktop in macOS Screen Sharing, 2026-11-24), one wheel notch on a 60x40 spreadsheet shifted rows by 5: the diff printed 426 of 443 lines, while only about 84 cells were newly visible. With no action between reads the diff was empty (OCR is stable on a static screen). Fix: when most matched texts moved by one common offset, report it once (for example 'scrolled: 330 lines moved up 70px') and print only texts not on the previous screen; items that moved by some other offset still print. Unit-test on synthetic before/after arrays shaped like a scrolled grid, including OCR variants (O for 0) and 1-2 px jitter.
acceptance_criteria: A unit test with a grid shifted by a common offset gets a diff that names only the newly visible texts plus one line giving the shift; a static screen still prints no change; npm test passes.
close_reason: Merged in PR #29

title: Add a test that examples/ and its README table stay in sync
description:
**What**
Each script in `examples/` must start with a `// ` description line (`nostrings scripts` shows it) and have a row in the table in `examples/README.md`; each row must point at a real file. Nothing enforces this, so a new example can ship without a row or a description. Add a test that reads the directory and the README.

**Where**
- `test/unit.test.mjs`, or a new `test/examples.test.mjs` (then add it to the `test` script in `package.json`)
- Read only: `examples/README.md`

**Done when**
- A new test, `examples: every script has a description and a README row`, passes under `npm test`.
- Every `examples/*.js` first line starts with `// ` and has text after it.
- Every `*.js` appears as a link in the README table, and every linked `.js` exists.
- Adding an empty `examples/zz.js` locally makes the test fail with a message naming `zz.js`.

**Size:** Small. One file, about 25 lines, plain `node:fs`.
close_reason: Merged in PR #27

title: Test that saved-script listing handles odd files
description:

**Where**

**Done when**

**Size:** Small. One file, about 25 lines, no GUI.

title: Add a unit test that the action log records route and error
description:
**What**
Every GUI action writes one line to `actions.log`. The line carries the `route` the action took, and on failure the error `code`. No test covers this, so a refactor could drop the fields unnoticed. Add a test that runs actions on a fake backend and checks the logged entries.

**Where**
- `test/unit.test.mjs` (add the test; the `activeApp` helper near line 227 collects log entries)
- Read only: where the line is written. Today that is `#act` in `src/api.mjs`; if PR #17 has merged, it is the broker in `src/broker.mjs`.

**Done when**
- A new test, `action log lines carry route on success and error code on failure`, passes under `npm test`.
- Success: an action on a backend that returns `{ route: "fake" }` logs `route` and no `error`.
- Failure: a backend that throws with `code: "not_visible"` logs `error` with that code, and the call still rejects.
- Removing the route from the log call locally makes the test fail.

**Size:** Small. One file, about 30 lines, no GUI.
close_reason: Merged in PR #27

title: getAXState({root}) to expand one folded outline subtree
description:
**What:** A large tree prints as an outline whose folded lines end in `(+N inside)`, but there is no way to print just one folded subtree. The only choices are `{full: true}`, which prints every element (often thousands of lines), or `find()`/`nodes()`, which return data and no tree. Add `getAXState({root: index})` to print the subtree under one element, with the same outline limit and diffing.

**Evidence:** `src/api.mjs:291-292` builds the outline and the `(+N inside)` marker, and the only escape it offers is `{full: true}` (`src/api.mjs:315`). agent-desktop documents this exact flow for dense apps: "use `--skeleton --compact` to map the app, then `--root <ref>` to drill into one region" (https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop).

**Why it matters:** Mail, Xcode, Finder lists and browsers go over 250 elements. Today an agent that needs one folded region either reads the whole tree, at a large token cost, or writes `nodes()` filtering code by hand. This fits the diffs-over-screenshots design and is not on the roadmap's token list.

**Done when:** A unit test in `test/unit.test.mjs` uses a fake backend with a tree of more than 250 elements. `getAXState({root: i})` on a folded element prints only that element and its descendants, with no line from outside the subtree, and a second identical call prints `no change`. `docs/api.md` documents `root`.

**Size:** medium (a session).

<!-- discovery: scout B -->
close_reason: Fixed on overhaul/init; npm test 26/26

title: nostrings script args drop leading zeros: code=012345 becomes 12345
description:
**What:** `nostrings script <name> key=value` turns every value that looks numeric into a Number. Leading zeros are lost and blanks become 0, so a one-time code, a ZIP code or an all-digit adb serial reaches the script changed.

**Evidence:** `src/scripts.mjs:75`, `raw !== "" && !Number.isNaN(Number(raw)) ? Number(raw) : raw`. Run here: `parseArgPairs(["code=012345","zip=02134","serial=0123456789","x= "])` returns `{ code: 12345, zip: 2134, serial: 123456789, x: 0 }`. `test/unit.test.mjs:378` only checks `a=2`.

**Why it matters:** Saved scripts get rerun from a shell with no model watching. The shipped examples take `serial`, `text` and codes (`examples/phone-code-to-mac.js`, `examples/textedit-note.js`), so a changed value gets typed or used without anyone seeing it.

**Done when:** A unit test asserts `parseArgPairs(["code=012345","x= "])` deep-equals `{ code: "012345", x: " " }`, so only canonical numbers convert (`String(Number(raw)) === raw`), and `npm test` passes. `docs/cli.md` says which values convert.

**Size:** small (under an hour).

<!-- discovery: scout A -->
close_reason: Fixed on overhaul/init; npm test 26/26

title: Horizontal background scroll (dx): retest on a remote-desktop viewer
description: A field run on a remote-desktop viewer (2026-10-29) found scroll(target,{dx:15}) had no effect on a remote table while dy worked; scrollbar-arrow clicks worked. Point and fixed-point axis-2 deltas are now set (2acf938) but not retried on a remote-desktop viewer.
acceptance_criteria: scroll(target,{dx}) moves a wide table horizontally in a remote-desktop viewer in the background.
notes: 2026-11-24 retest on a headless Linux VNC desktop viewed in macOS Screen Sharing (standard connection): scroll(target,{dx:15}) does not move a remote spreadsheet, dy does. Isolated: (1) horizontal wheel sent on the remote side itself moves the sheet, so the target handles it; (2) the same background dx moves a local Numbers sheet both ways, so the helper's axis-2 events work; (3) the remote X server receives only vertical wheel buttons from Screen Sharing, and a real two-finger sideways swipe by the maintainer also does not scroll. So macOS Screen Sharing drops horizontal wheel; this viewer cannot validate the bead. Still open for the original viewer type. Workaround for agents: scrollbar arrows or arrow keys.

acceptance_criteria: pressKey('Escape', {window}) closes the menu within 0.5 s in the background.
notes: 2026-11-24: still reproduces; documented as a limit (Gecko popups ignore background Escape; pressing the button again closes it). Lead: keys aimed at the popup's own window id closed it once.
